newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU ENDS FLAT VS DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU ENDS FLAT VS DOLLAR.

text.p: Romania's leu closed flat on Thursday with dealers' quotes ranging from 7,000/100 to 8,200/300 and operators said they expected it to weaken slightly over the next week.
Operators said they expected Wednesday's attempt to prop the leu, when the central bank (BNR) sold "several million dollars", to have a short-lived effect.

"It appears the market has already swallowed the BNR dollars. Trading at 8,200/300 was more intense by the end of the day and this makes me believe the leu will weaken and the situation will go back to square one," a dealer said.
The intervention, on which the BNR declined to comment, made the leu some 1,500 stronger over the course of Tuesday's trading.

The BNR's move, combined with an increase in interest rates by several state-run commercial banks, generated a leu shortage on the market and apparently restored public confidence in the national currency.
People queued at reatil shops to exchange their dollars into lei to make deposits at commercial banks.

"One should also have in mind the fact that by next week there will be up to 600 billion lei on the market coming from T-bills so banks will start again to remain on long positions for dollars," another dealer said.
On Thursday, leu prices at licenced money changing bureaux -- also hit by leu shortages -- hovered at around 7,500/8,100, against the dollar, same as Wednesday's levels.
The reference rate has clung to 7,744 to the dollar since Monday, when the BNR had been expected to announce a new computation method for the rate. But the BNR postponed the announcement.
